rationale: Cheapest acceptable model for Week 1 scope: a bounded single-turn Q&A endpoint whose deliverable is a working /ask contract with observable tokens_used/cost_usd, not answer quality tuned across models. gpt-4.1-nano is cheaper than the prior selection (gpt-4o-mini) on both input ($0.10 vs $0.15 per 1M) and output ($0.40 vs $0.60 per 1M), and has exactly one unambiguous pricing record in config/model-pricing.json. Revisit once the capstone's retrieval/evidence pipeline (Week 2+) makes response quality, not just cost, a load-bearing evaluation dimension.
notes:
2026-09-13: switched from gpt-4o-mini, matching the same-day switch in ../ai-eng-bootcamp.vera/config/model-selection.json. That file's notes flagged a real bug this project shared verbatim: pricing_config.py's latest_pricing_for() picked the 'latest' price record by effective_from date only, ignoring service_tier — several models (gpt-5-nano, gpt-5.4-nano, gpt-5-mini) have both a 'standard' and a 'flex' record sharing the same effective_from date, making that pick arbitrary. Fixed here (ahead of VERA, which deferred it) by defaulting latest_pricing_for to service_tier='standard'. Also added supported_models (this list) as the single source of truth for every allowed model name across main.py, demo_page.py, and the startup pricing check, replacing a hardcoded Python Literal that had to be kept in sync with this file by hand.

selected_model/supported_models above answer 'what can a caller explicitly force via a per-request model= override?' — unchanged by the addition below, and still OpenAI-only. provider_chain answers a different question: 'what serves the request when no override is given?' Added 2026-09-13, closing Module 1.D2 (provider landscape beyond OpenAI): a free-tier-first, paid-fallback-last chain, tried in order, skipping any entry whose credentials aren't configured. Every entry's structured_output field is only 'strict' when independently confirmed from that provider's OWN documentation (not an aggregator) to support schema-constrained output the way /ask, /summarize, and /analyze-sentiment need it — this distinction turned out to matter immediately: an early pass at this research trusted a secondary benchmark claiming 'Groq passes structured output on every model,' which Groq's own docs directly contradict (strict mode is limited to openai/gpt-oss-20b, openai/gpt-oss-120b, and qwen/qwen3.8-27b). Only Groq and Gemini are marked 'strict' here as a result; Mistral/OpenRouter/SambaNova/Cloudflare Workers AI are 'unverified' for structured output and only participate in /ask/stream's freeform chain (no schema requirement there) until independently confirmed and promoted. None of these entries carry a price: a free-tier allowance (see each entry's free_entitlement_* fields) is a different fact from a model's canonical per-token price, never collapsed into a fake $0 — see pricing_config.ProviderConfig's docstring. Real canonical prices for the two 'strict' entries actually used for cost_usd (Groq, Gemini) are tracked as ordinary records in config/model-pricing.json, sourced from secondary aggregators after this session's own primary-source pricing-page fetches 404'd — flagged in those records' own notes as needing a final reconfirmation, not presented as more certain than it is.

provider_chain.rationale: Confirmed directly from Groq's own docs (not an aggregator) to support strict JSON-schema structured output — one of only three models Groq lists for that mode. OpenAI-SDK-compatible via base_url, no bespoke client needed. Also has a 30-requests/minute burst limit alongside the 1,000/day figure tracked here.
provider_chain.notes: Rate limits per https://console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits. Pricing (config/model-pricing.json) sourced from secondary aggregators after console.groq.com/docs/pricing returned 404 on direct fetch — needs reconfirmation before being treated as authoritative. reasoning_effort=low added 2026-09-25 (p3m3 #50): gpt-oss's hidden reasoning shares the 1,000-token completion budget. At the default effort it used a median 776 (max 995) completion tokens on the /ask prompt, and intermittently failed with 400 json_validate_failed; at low, a median 200.

provider_chain.rationale: Google's own OpenAI-compatibility docs demonstrate .parse() with a Pydantic schema against this exact model. Highest free rate limit (60 RPM) of any candidate in this chain.
provider_chain.notes: Exact current free-tier model ID drifted once already during this session's own research (gemini-2.5-flash -> gemini-3.8-flash) — reconfirm against Google's current docs before relying on this string long-term.

provider_chain.rationale: Mistral's free 'Experiment' tier covers all API models under one rate-limited allowance rather than a single distinct free model, so this is a representative small/cheap pick, not a Mistral-designated 'free model.' API-level JSON-schema mode exists per Mistral's docs, but per-model strict-mode support wasn't independently confirmed this session — usable in /ask/stream's chain now, promotable to structured once confirmed.
provider_chain.notes: structured_output left 'unverified' deliberately, not assumed strict.

provider_chain.rationale: Aggregates 25+ free models behind one key — useful as a fallback if a single upstream free provider is down. The free-model list changes regularly per OpenRouter's own description; this specific model ID needs reconfirming against OpenRouter's live free-models page before relying on it.
provider_chain.notes: structured_output left 'unverified': OpenRouter passes response_format through to whichever upstream model serves the request, so support depends on that model, not confirmed independently here.

provider_chain.rationale: Confirmed OpenAI-SDK-compatible base_url from SambaNova's own docs. Free-tier allowance figures for SambaNova varied across sources checked this session (200,000 tokens/day in one pass, 20 requests/day in another) — tracked here as the more conservative figure, but flagged as needing reconfirmation, not treated as settled.
provider_chain.notes: structured_output left 'unverified' — not independently confirmed this session.

provider_chain.rationale: Confirmed OpenAI-compatible endpoint from Cloudflare's own docs. Needs two credentials (an API token and an account ID), one more than every other entry in this chain. Entitlement is measured in Cloudflare's own 'Neurons' unit, not requests or tokens directly — deliberately tracked as its own unit rather than converted to a guessed request/token equivalent.
provider_chain.notes: base_url's {CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID} placeholder is substituted at request time by providers._resolve_base_url() from the CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID env var named in extra_env above. Untestable end-to-end without real Cloudflare credentials, which aren't configured in this project's .env.

provider_chain.rationale: Always-trusted terminal fallback: if every free provider above is unconfigured, cooling down, or fails, this is the paid path the assignment's own wallet-safety controls already cover. Matches selected_model above.
provider_chain.notes: No free_entitlement fields: this is the paid path by design, not a free tier.
